messages:
michael: heads up — noticed a weird regression in tokenizer behavior on the new int8-quant build during the multilingual eval sweep.

michael: specifically, ZWJ emoji sequences (family + gender combos) and some CJK punctuation adjacent to emoji are being split into extra tokens, inflating token counts and hurting chrF/bleu on small translation tests.

anya: ugh, any quick repro?

michael: yes. short repros from the eval set:
```
input: "👩‍👩‍👧‍👦 今天我很高兴。"
old-tokenizer: ["👩‍👩‍👧‍👦", " 今天", " 我", " 很", " 高兴", "。"]
new-tokenizer: ["👩", "‍", "👩", "‍", "👧", "‍", "👦", " 今天", " 我", " 很", " 高兴", " 。"]
```

michael: same for Japanese + ZWJ emoji: it splits the emoji into ZWJ fragments and attaches punctuation as separate tokens where before punctuation was merged in predictable ways.

zhang: hmm that looks like a tokenizer merge-table change, not quant math. Did we switch tokenization codepath or merge rules in the micropatch?

kevin: I pulled the staging tarball, the only tokenizer diff in the PR was a fallback to the new byte-level postprocess for unknown grapheme sequences (PR #4823). It was supposed to be a no-op for known emojis, but maybe ZWJ handling got affected.

anya: also seeing model scoring dip on short-form zh->en and ja->en where emoji + sentence punctuation present. Example metrics (staging-int8 vs baseline fp16):
- zh->en BLEU: baseline 21.7 -> staging-int8 20.0
- ja->en chrF: baseline 0.542 -> staging-int8 0.520
Token count per sentence increased ~+12% for the affected bucket.

michael: eval-bot post from the run: 
```
EVAL RUN 2026-03-19 14:02:13
models: redwood-v2-small-int8 (staging)
benchmarks: multilingual-shortform-v1
failure_mode: tokenization/ZWJ-splitting
notes: increased latency ~3% due to longer sequences
```

kevin: deploy-bot shows we rolled the int8 artifact that includes both the runtime and the tokenizer binary. Could revert tokenizer binary only to test.

deploy-bot: rollback available: artifact redwood-v2-small-int8@build-20260319-0634 — will revert if you confirm.

zhang: quick triage plan: 1) reproduce locally with the tokenizer binary from build vs previous; 2) compare byte->unicode normalization tables; 3) run tokenization-only diff to isolate merge rule changes.

anya: i'll run the tokenization-only diffs against a curated set of ZWJ, emoji sequences, and CJK punctuation. assigning to me for now.

michael: thanks. if it's just postprocessing we can patch quickly. if it's a changed grapheme clustering fallback that upstream depended on, might need a small patch plus a re-run of calibration for quant buckets.

anya: quick note — found one oddity: the new postprocess maps U+200D (ZWJ) to an explicit zero-width token in the byte-level path for unknown graphemes. previously ZWJ was swallowed into a single emoji token. reproducer: "👩‍❤️‍👩" -> new path: ["👩", "200D", "❤️", "200D", "👩"] which explains the split.

kevin: that mapping was added to handle some edge case in Indic scripts where ZWJ must be preserved. We accidentally enabled it for the byte-level fallback unconditionally. Fix proposal: apply mapping only when script != Emoji and when grapheme cluster length > 1? or better: keep existing emoji table precedence.

zhang: agree — prefer a narrower rule. Also let's add regression test in tokenization tests covering common emoji ZWJ sequences plus mixed CJK punctuation cases.

michael: adding a perf note: the inflated token counts also blow up caching hit rates on prefix cache (observed drop from 78% -> 61% on affected flows). So this is both quality and cost regression.

anya: patched a local build with emoji precedence restored and ran tokenization-only unit tests — green. pushing a quick fix to staging, will run full evals (tokenization + translation) in ~20m.

eval-bot: staging run finished: zh->en BLEU now 21.6 (within noise), ja->en chrF 0.541, token inflation gone (<1% change).

michael: excellent. can we add a small test in the quant bring-up checklist to run tokenization-only diffs whenever runtime or tokenizer binary changes?

kevin: yes — created ticket INF-1217 to add tokenization-diff gate and a small curated emoji/cjk suite.

anya: will follow up with the patch PR link and the failing test case added.

michael: thanks everyone. leaving this thread pinned until the staging->prod push completes. :thumbsup:
